result: No confirmed blocker in the reviewed issuance, provider matching and capability propagation paths.
scope: Provider construction before with_config and final provider snapshot at builder injection.
ThreadManager default None, one-time unique-Arc injection, per-spawn overwrite of the private typed context.
Session context extraction and strong-Arc ownership in ModelClient.
Both internal metadata filtering decisions in ModelClient and public hidden test-support forwarding.
findings: Lease issuance requires built-in OpenAI fixture provenance, exact configured provider identity and literal normalized HTTP loopback /v1 with an explicit nonzero port, no credentials/query/fragment in the URL. Custom provider name, auth/header/wire or endpoint changes fail the equality check.
The five allowed configuration changes affect transport behavior. The finalized complete provider is cloned into the lease, so subsequent changes to any of those fields also fail matching.
New managers and clients default to None. Every manager spawn replaces the private FixtureMetadataContext; copied extension attachments cannot independently authorize a different manager.

Child/resumed sessions retain only their owning manager's lease when its full config matches. ModelClient holds a strong Arc and checks exact provider plus exact request endpoint at use; no global URL registry or environment/config switch was found in these reviewed changes.
The existing normal endpoint acceptance helper is still called before the explicit lease path. This review did not independently re-read or re-prove the unchanged helper module.
Debug output omits provider values and endpoint. No lease serialization was present.
boundaries: The hidden test-support entry point is intentionally compiled and publicly callable by Rust consumers of test_support; doc(hidden) is not a security boundary. The reviewed grant is an explicit test API capability, not a claim that arbitrary Rust code cannot construct test fixtures.
Provider/endpoint equality is not cryptographic authentication of the process currently listening on that port. The review makes no server-identity or unbounded network-lifetime claim.
Only selected propagation regions of the large existing files were reviewed, not the entire client/session implementation.
The proposed eight unit tests and four integration lifecycle tests were not independently read or executed in this review. Actual full native qualification remains required.
